To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the beliefs researchers hold, the technological artifacts that they create, and their evaluation routines for judging those artifacts, are all mutually reinforcing.

the beliefs researchers hold, the technological artifacts researchers create, and the evaluation routines researchers use for assessing their own and others' work, interact in a reciprocal manner over time to produce a technology.

the beliefs researchers hold, the technological artifacts researchers create, and the evaluation routines researchers use for judging their artifacts are all interrelated and influence the direction of technological change.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the processes that shape the beliefs that researchers hold about what a technology can or cannot do and how well it meets with their prior expectations.
how the social and cognitive aspects of technology evolution unfold and influence one another over time.
the social and cognitive factors that influence the evolution of new technologies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a new technology is the outcome of a complex process involving the interplay among individual beliefs, technological artifacts, and evaluation routines.
a technology evolves through a series of cycles of inversion at the individual level and institutionalization at the shared cognition level.
the model presented in this paper has been tested in a historical case and has been found to be valid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the social and cognitive dynamics of the technology evolution process are complex and can lead to unexpected results, even when there are clear and compelling technical advantages.
the evolution of technology is a process that unfolds over time and is driven by the interplay of social and cognitive processes.

we believe that a technology's evolution is not just a technical process, but a socio-cognitive one as well, and that the socio-cognitive aspects are as important in shaping the evolution of the technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
researchers who want to be on the winning side must be ready and willing to abandon their own realities and join the new emerging reality.
the process of technological development is not simply one of technical problem solving. It is also one of social problem solving.

the social and cognitive dynamics of technological evolution can be understood by examining the interrelationships between the artifacts that are being developed, the routines used to evaluate those artifacts, and the beliefs about what is and what is not feasible that guide the development of both artifacts and routines.
